# Minimum Operations to Make Array Sum Divisible by K.

@example The piles hold 19 stones; taking 3 of them leaves 16, a multiple of 4.
[8,5,6]
4
=> 3

@example The total, 60, is already a multiple of 6.
[10,20,30]
6
=> 0

@example The total, 7, is below 10, so the only multiple in reach is 0: every stone has to go.
[2,1,4]
10
=> 7

# The smallest input: one stone, and k = 1.
[1]
1
=> 0

# With k = 1 every total is a multiple.
[1000,999,7]
1
=> 0

# A single pile, partly taken.
[17]
5
=> 2

# A single pile smaller than k: all of it goes.
[9]
100
=> 9

# The total, 23, is 11 above a multiple of 12. Adding 1 stone would be
# shorter, but stones can only be taken away.
[20,3]
12
=> 11

# The total, 51, is 1 above a multiple of 10.
[25,26]
10
=> 1

# Each pile is 9 above a multiple of 10 on its own, but only the total
# counts: 36 needs 6 moves, not 4 * 9.
[9,9,9,9]
10
=> 6

# The answer, 9, is more than any one pile holds, so the moves have to be
# spread over several piles.
[4,5,6,7]
13
=> 9

# The total equals k.
[40,60]
100
=> 0

# The largest possible answer: k = 100 and a total of 1999.
[999,1000]
100
=> 99
